title: GPIO15 wait_pulse delay path: stock vs openCFW static compare, ITCM loop fix
scope: Static compare of wait_pulse/delay_us, then make openCFW's spin loop use the same ITCM 0x40 overlay as stock. Rebuild apollo-main (incremental am_hal_utils + relink). Re-run version-match and mismatch sims. No hardware flash. NVM not in this step. SoC is Apollo510 (Ambiq MRAM/ITCM split; the request said Apollo4).

wait_pulse.stock: 0x52e854, (duration*1000)/udiv 33 iterations, each gpio15=0, bl 0x491102(16), gpio15=1, bl 0x491102(16). duration 40 => 1212 iterations.
wait_pulse.opencfw: 0x0046ad80, same 1212 count via umull magic 0x3e0f83e1>>3 (= /33), same gpio15=0, delay_us(16), gpio15=1, delay_us(16). Early-out if duration*1000 < 33 (not taken for 40).
wait_pulse.gpio_hal: Stock uses 0x480f0c pinconfig and 0x480fd6 write; openCFW uses am_hal_gpio_pinconfig / am_hal_gpio_state_write. Possible extra non-dominant overhead; the designed pulse width is delay_us(16)+delay_us(16).

calibration.clock_reg: 0x40021000, bits [4:3] (stock ubfx #3,#2 cmp #2; openCFW and #24 cmp #16 — equivalent). SDK names this PWRCTRL MCUPERFSTATUS: LP 96 MHz vs HP 250 MHz.
calibration.loop_assumption: 3 cycles per iteration (HAL comment; 32*3=96 cycles/us at 96 MHz)

itcm_overlay.stock: IAR LZ77 row installs this 24-byte helper at 0x40. am_hal_delay_us 0x4807a0 ends in bl 0x40 (16-bit bne countdown).
itcm_overlay.opencfw_before: g2c_gnu_init copies the same 24 bytes to 0x40 (Nov 11 overlay). The Nov 11 overlay therefore covers the stock delay loop, but openCFW am_hal_delay_us did not call it.
itcm_overlay.opencfw_before_spin: br_util_delay_cycles at 0x00600744 in MRAM (.itcm_text was merged into MRAM .text by g2-apollo-main.ld). Loop is subs; bne.w (32-bit) to the global symbol; bx lr.

period_estimate.per_pulse: two delay_us(16) plus two GPIO writes, nominally ~32 us plus GPIO HAL
period_estimate.opencfw_before_if_icache_hits: A 32-bit bne.w in a 6-byte MRAM loop may be 3 or 4 cycles once cached. Four cycles would stretch each half-pulse by about 33% (~21 us vs ~16 us). Estimate, not measured.
period_estimate.opencfw_before_if_uncached: The HAL places this routine in .itcm_text specifically so fetch bypasses I-cache and stays 3 cycles. Uncached MRAM wait states on a 6-byte loop would make the pulse longer, not shorter. A 2-3x stretch is a plausible order of magnitude without a measured wait-state number from the Apollo510 datasheet.
period_estimate.sim_limitation: Renode is not cycle-accurate for MRAM vs ITCM wait states. The re-runs are functional regressions, not a silicon period proof.

fix.g2-apollo-main.ld: itcm_countdown_loop = 0x00000041 (Thumb entry of the overlay countdown)
fix.linked: br_util_delay_cycles at 0x00600744 is b.w 0x40; am_hal_delay_us (0x0060075c) still bhi.w br_util_delay_cycles; calibration unchanged

image.note: 8 bytes smaller than the 22 Nov recovery image (3,818,880 B); shrink is the shorter trampoline.

version_match_8s.note: Identical HCI and frames to the 6:08 AM CST advertising-disarm CHIPREV=0x22 openCFW run. Arm then disarm still observed. recover_stop not entered on the version-match path.

mismatch_8s.note: recover_stop still completes after the trampoline (0x40 is preloaded and later installed by g2c_gnu_init). DFU erase 0xFD06 remains unmodeled.

app_dead.software_gap_closed: OpenCFW's GPIO15 pulse spin loop now uses the same ITCM 16-bit countdown as stock. The previously evidenced MRAM/bne.w difference is no longer present in the image.
app_dead.still_hypothesis: Whether that difference (or remaining GPIO HAL / delay-prologue differences) caused the app-dead temples is still unproven. Official 2.2.6.10 came up, so recover_stop either was not entered or completed under official timing. No factory trim dump and no GPIO15 traces.

next: Implement EM9305 NVM program/erase starting with HCI 0xFD06 EMSMM_NVMEraseMain, then the mismatch pair through a completed DFU, then (3) case-reply disarm with a pogo product-test frame.
